subject: Next steps: purchase-route validation, paperwork & SOC 2 evidence
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Kirsten Hale <kirsten@novaprospect.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: procurement options & security checklist

Hi Kirsten —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so your procurement team can evaluate the path to purchase: 

- Commercial paths: 1) PO (standard for mid-market buyers) 2) Credit card via self-serve (faster) 3) Marketplace (Azure/GCP) if you want consolidated billing.
- Paperwork we typically expect: DPA + SOW / PO template + any vendor onboarding form you require.
- Security gating: SOC 2 Type II summary and a completed security questionnaire (DDQ) if you run one. I can share our SOC 2 summary and a short SOC2 one-pager.

Can you confirm which commercial path Procurement prefers (PO vs card vs marketplace) and who in your team we should loop in? Also, does Procurement require any specific contract terms redlines up front (data residency, indemnity caps)?

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preferred purchase route and procurement contact.
2) We send DPA + SOC2 summary + a PO template for your legal/procurement.
3) If you have a DDQ, share a copy and we’ll start answering.

I’ll loop in our commercial lead (Ben) and contracts (Marissa) once you confirm so we can prepare the right paperwork.

Thanks —

Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (summary), PO_template.docx (sample template)
From: Kirsten Hale <kirsten@novaprospect.com>

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side:

- Procurement is leaning toward a PO route (we run quarterly vendor cycles and prefer PO + net30).
- Please send the DPA and SOC2 evidence; legal will want to review the DPA and our team will run a quick redline review.
- We do have a standard DDQ (attached) — it’s not exhaustive but will likely flag questions around encryption in transit/at rest, access controls, and data deletion.

Looping in procurement@novaprospect.com and Ethan (security) to confirm intake steps.

Can you also confirm: does Redwood require data residency guarantees for US-only customers, or do you offer region pinning for hosted deployments?

Kirsten Hale
Head of GTM Ops, NovaProspect
kirsten@novaprospect.com

Marissa / Ben —

Forwarding Kirsten’s response. Procurement prefers PO + net30 and they attached a DDQ. Two asks for us:

1) Marissa — can you prepare a draft DPA and confirm whether we should propose standard Redwood terms or the redline-light option we use for SMB mid-market? Also attach the SOC 2 summary and the standard PO template (I’ve attached SOC2-summary.pdf & PO_template.docx for context).
2) Ben — can you price a quarterly commit SKU vs pay-as-you-go? They’ll evaluate both but prefer predictable spend. If we can show a recommended commit that lowers per-token costs that’ll help.

Kirsten also asked about data residency / region pinning for US-only customers — what is the quick answer we can provide?

I’ll reply to Kirsten once we have the DPA + SOC2 and a suggested commercial option.

Thanks —
Logan
